description: Hardware Hacking Village focuses on physical hardware reverse engineering, embedded firmware extraction, keystroke injection attacks, USB HID exploitation, and AVR microcontrollers.

talks.title: Walkthrough of DC28 HHV Challenge Solutions
talks.teaser: HHV challenge designer rehr presents the official solutions to all five DEF CON 28 Hardware Hacking Village challenges, demystifying hardware reverse engineering.
talks.summary:
The DEF CON 28 Hardware Hacking Village Challenges

During DEF CON 28, the Hardware Hacking Village released five progressively difficult hardware reverse engineering challenges that tested firmware extraction, signal analysis, and protocol decoding.

Demystifying Hardware Reverse Engineering Solutions

rehr walks through the complete solution steps for each challenge, showing how only three attendees solved all five problems during the conference.

Analyzing Firmware, Logic Traces, and Serial Protocols

The author details using logic analyzers, UART and SPI sniffing, and disassemblers to bypass hardware security checks and extract embedded flags.

Key Takeaways for Aspiring Hardware Hackers

The presentation provides methodologies and open-source tool recommendations for hackers looking to practice hardware CTF solving.

talks.title: The Black Box and the Brain Box: When Electronics & Deception Collide
talks.teaser: Gigs explores the intersection of electronics and deception, investigating the pseudoscience and electronic design flaws of polygraph and biofeedback machines.
talks.summary:
The Historical Mystification of Electrical Devices

Throughout history, electrical instruments have been imbued with an aura of infallible truth, leading to widespread reliance on questionable electronic detection devices.

Gigs examines the analog circuits and signal acquisition hardware behind galvanic skin response (GSR), polygraphs, and commercial brainwave (EEG) headsets.

Exposing Vulnerabilities in Deception Detection Tech

The author demonstrates technical flaws, physiological bypasses, and sensor spoofing techniques that undermine the credibility of electronic lie detection.

Ethical Implications of Electronic Interrogation

The presentation critiques the use of pseudoscientific electronic devices in legal, employment, and law enforcement interrogation contexts.

talks.title: Hardware Hacking 101: Rogue Keyboards & Spy Cables
talks.teaser: Federico Lucifredi demonstrates keystroke injection attacks, exploiting OS trust in USB HID devices to execute 1,000 WPM payloads via weaponized cables.
talks.summary:
The Inherent Trust Model of USB Human Interface Devices (HID)

Operating systems automatically trust connected USB keyboards and mice without requiring administrative authentication or cryptographic device validation.

Deconstructing Keystroke Injection Attacks

Federico Lucifredi demonstrates how malicious microcontrollers disguised as USB cables or flash drives inject pre-programmed keystrokes at over 1,000 words per minute.

Live Demonstration of Host Compromise and Evasion

Lucifredi showcases launching hidden terminal shells, disabling antivirus defenses, and exfiltrating corporate data in seconds using weaponized USB hardware.

Defending Endpoints Against Malicious USB Devices

The author reviews defensive countermeasures—including USB port whitelisting, physical port blockers, and behavioral HID typing-speed heuristics.

talks.title: The PortaProg Project: Portable Multi-Protocol Firmware Programmer
talks.teaser: Bradan Lane introduces PortaProg, an open-source portable hardware programmer for flashing Atmel AVR microcontrollers via ISP and UPDI in the field.
talks.summary:
The Need for Standalone Field Firmware Programmers

Hardware hackers and embedded developers frequently need to reprogram AVR microcontrollers in the field without carrying bulky computers and programmer dongles.

Introducing the Open-Source PortaProg

Bradan Lane presents PortaProg, a compact, battery-powered hardware programmer capable of flashing firmware across diverse Atmel chips.

Multi-Protocol Support: ISP, UPDI, and High-Voltage Programming

Lane explains how the device handles In-System Programming (ISP), Unified Program and Debug Interface (UPDI), fuse byte modification, and EEPROM read/write.

Benchtop and Field Deployment Workflows

The author demonstrates flashing firmware directly from PortaProg's on-board SPIFFS storage, providing open-source hardware schematics and code.

talks.title: A Lazy Solve of HHV Challenge 6: Radare2, AVR, & 7-Segment Displays
talks.teaser: Ben Gardiner walks through solving HHV Challenge 6, combining Radare2 AVR disassembly, logic analyzer decoding in Sigrok, and 7-segment display reverse engineering.
talks.summary:
Approaching Hardware CTF Challenges Pragmatically

Solving hardware hacking challenges requires chaining disparate skills—from embedded firmware disassembly to digital signal decoding—into a cohesive workflow.

Disassembling AVR Firmware with Radare2

Ben Gardiner demonstrates analyzing an unknown microcontroller firmware dump using Radare2, mapping AVR register operations and interrupt vector tables.

Decoding Digital Signal Traces in Sigrok

Gardiner illustrates using PulseView and Sigrok to capture, inspect, and decode multiplexed GPIO pin toggles driving 7-segment LED displays.

Extracting the Embedded Flag from Display Logic

The walkthrough shows how correlating disassembly control flow with decoded LED pin states recovers the hidden challenge flag.
